finding: src/anomaly/readme.py:36 README projection deletes journalist-authored content that exactly matches the legacy Outputs block.
rationale: A journalist-edited regular README can contain this exact unmarked section, and public completion, completed-case resume, or invalidation reaches the unconditional global replacement, silently deleting user-authored content in direct conflict with the preservation acceptance criterion.

evidence.output: project_readme accepts any existing non-symlink README, removes the marked Anomaly block, then unconditionally executes .replace(_OUTPUTS, ""); Python str.replace removes every exact occurrence, with no ownership or position guard.

The public run_workflow entry repeatedly calls load_snapshot; completed P7 snapshots call project_readme, successful P7 sealing calls it, and invalidation from a previously completed P7 calls it again. The destructive branch is therefore reachable during ordinary completion, restart, and invalidation flows.

resume_case/_load_case validates case.json and progress but imposes no README-content restriction; the initial README is ordinary journalist-facing Markdown. No upstream guard makes an exact unmarked Outputs section impossible.
